pathwayLabel: Full New Application Required — No Reciprocity or Exam Waiver Available for C-20
examName: CSLB C-20 (Warm-Air Heating, Ventilating and Air-Conditioning) trade exam — no waiver route exists for this classification
steps: Florida is not one of CSLB's five reciprocal-agreement states (Arizona, Louisiana, Mississippi, Nevada, North Carolina), so no state-to-state reciprocity waiver applies.

Unlike general contracting, C-20 has no broader exam-waiver alternative either: CSLB's NASCLA exam waiver is restricted to the General Building classification only and does not cover C-20 — confirmed directly from CSLB's own reciprocity page.

Even among CSLB's actual reciprocal partner states, C-20 coverage is inconsistent: only Arizona and Nevada have license classifications that map to C-20 on CSLB's official Reciprocal Classifications List. Louisiana and North Carolina have no C-20 mapping at all, despite being reciprocal partners for other classifications.
Because none of this applies to a Florida license, a full original CSLB application is required: document four years of qualifying C-20 experience, and pass the C-20 trade exam.
Pay the CSLB single-classification application fee ($450).
Await processing — CSLB does not publish a guaranteed timeline; budget for several weeks to a few months.
notes: Confirmed directly from CSLB's official Reciprocal Classifications List (live-fetched): Florida is absent entirely, and even Louisiana and North Carolina — two of CSLB's five general reciprocal states — have no C-20 mapping at all. Only Arizona (C-39/C-39R/K-39/K-79/L-39/L-79) and Nevada (C-1f/C-21) map to C-20. Separately, CSLB's NASCLA-exam waiver (which does help a Florida contractor for General Building specifically, see the sourced florida-california contractor record) is explicitly restricted to 'CSLB General Building classification only' per CSLB's own reciprocity page — it does not extend to C-20, so there is no waiver alternative for HVAC the way there is for general contracting. The $450 fee and 4-year experience figure are CSLB's standard original-application requirements (same source used for the contractor pair), not classification-specific, so reused here rather than re-derived.
